beats.text: Excel was quietly corrupting gene names in published science.
beats.note: A study of papers from 2005 to 2015 found 19.6% of those with Excel gene lists contained errors.
MARCH1 became 1-Mar. Excel read the gene symbols as dates.

beats.context: Renamed in 2020 by the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee, according to press reports, so that Excel would stop mistaking them for dates.

beats.note: SEPT2 is now SEPTIN2. The scientists changed the genes, not the software.

beats.text: It was easier to rename human genes than to change a spreadsheet.

beats.line: Even biology has to work around the software.
